title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows + optimize cache & parallelism
author: Amira Khatri
description: Motivation: our combined CI workflows have grown slow and brittle as we added more language matrixes and release automation steps. This PR splits responsibilities across smaller dedicated workflows (lint, unit/integration test, release) and applies cache and parallelism improvements to reduce runtime and flakiness. Goals: 1) reduce average CI wall time for PRs by ~40%, 2) make lint/test steps more cache-friendly and easier to rerun, 3) isolate release automation so it only runs on release tags or main branch merges. Changes are backwards-compatible with existing job names and retention; rollout will be gradual with canary repo settings. Summary of changes: - Split .github/workflows/ci.yml into three workflows: lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml. - Introduced a shared workflow template .github/workflows/templates/node-setup.yml for Node setup, caching, and matrix control. - Switched Node job matrices to node-version: [18, 20] for libraries and pinned action versions for reproducibility. - Implemented key-based cache keys: cache-{{ runner.os }}-pnpm-{{ hashFiles('**/pnpm-lock.yaml') }} and restored cache-on-failure heuristics. - Added test sharding for integration tests using matrix shards and deterministic seed to improve parallelism. - Reworked release workflow to only run on push tags and protected main merges; cleaned up release notes generation and artifact retention. - Small hygiene: removed legacy deprecated actions and consolidated common env vars in repository secrets. Testing: ran full CI on branch and validated with 6 canary PRs across redwood, redwood-sdk-python and redwood-examples. Observed median runtime reduction from ~27m -> ~16m for PRs. Checklist: - [x] split workflows and add templates - [x] preserve existing status checks names - [x] run canary PRs and validate caches - [x] update docs/CONTRIBUTING.md referencing new CI steps - [x] notify platform and infra channels; revert plan prepared (revert branch ci/revert/split-workflows) Related: ENG-4921 (CI perf epic) and ENG-4983 (release automation cleanup).

review_comments: Jonah Park: Looks good overall — can we avoid running the release workflow on deploy tags created by the old automation? I think we should ignore tags with prefix 'legacy/' to be safe.
Amira Khatri: Good call, added a conditional to ignore tags starting with legacy/ and added a short unit test for tag parsing.
Rae Chen: Cache key looks reasonable, but can we include an npm toolchain fingerprint in case pnpm behaves differently across runners?
Amira Khatri: Included runner.os and pnpm-lock hash; also added a static PNPM_VERSION repo secret and included it in the cache key to make the fingerprint explicit.
Liam O'Connor: Integration shard 3 failed intermittently on first run; suggest adding retry logic for flaky infra failures.
Amira Khatri: Added 2 retry attempts with exponential backoff for test shards and updated README note about test shard determinism.
release_notes: CI: split monolithic workflows into lint/test/release for faster PR feedback
CI: improved pnpm cache keys and added retry for flaky shards
CI: pinned action versions and Node matrix cleanup (18, 20)
